chunks: From him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from them, peace be upon them:

Regarding a newborn who has neither what men have nor what women have, except for a hole from which urine exits: upon which inheritance is he inherited? He said: 'If when he urinates his urine moves aside (separates), he is inherited with the inheritance of the male; and if when he urinates his urine does not move aside, he is inherited with the inheritance of the female.'
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite determined in Shia jurisprudence based on urine discharge?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in determining the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite (*khuntha*) based on observable physiological signs rather than internal anatomy. Specifically, it utilizes the behavior of urine discharge—whether it flows distinctly like a male or splashes like a female—as the decisive criterion for assigning either the male or female inheritance portion, reflecting the practical legal methodology of the Shia jurists.
